role_sought: Member of the Wiener Neustadt municipal council, ÖVP list
detail: Member of the municipal council from 1990 and re-elected at each election until 2015; the city was governed by the SPÖ until 2015, when the ÖVP took over the city government. The official results of these elections were not retrieved for this profile.

role_sought: Member of the National Council (ÖVP candidate, regional constituency Lower Austria South and Lower Austria state list)
detail: According to German Wikipedia, citing the Interior Ministry's candidate lists, he stood fifth on the ÖVP list in Lower Austria South and 51st on the Lower Austria list and missed out on a seat. He entered the National Council on 12 June 2019 as a replacement for Johann Rädler, who had been elected in 2017.

role_sought: Member of the National Council (ÖVP, regional constituency 3E Lower Austria South)
vote_share: ÖVP: 1,789,417 votes (37.5%) nationally; 48,568 votes (39.5%) in Lower Austria South, one regional seat
detail: Early election; the ÖVP under Sebastian Kurz came first. Stocker kept his seat for constituency 3E Lower Austria South.

role_sought: Member of the Wiener Neustadt municipal council (ÖVP list 'Bürgermeister-Team Klaus Schneeberger')
vote_share: ÖVP list: 45.0%, 19 of 40 seats (derived from the city's 2025 comparison figures)
detail: After the election he continued as first vice-mayor, responsible for finance and property management. The 2020 figures are derived from the official 2025 results published by the city, which state the changes against 2020 (ÖVP 35.8%, −9.2 points; 15 seats, −4).

role_sought: Member of the National Council (ÖVP lead candidate in Lower Austria South; 7th on the federal list)
vote_share: ÖVP: 1,282,734 votes (26.3%), 51 seats nationally; 33,728 votes (26.7%) and one regional seat in Lower Austria South
opponent: FPÖ (Herbert Kickl), first with 1,408,512 votes (28.8%) and 57 seats; in Lower Austria South the FPÖ won 42,144 votes (33.4%)
detail: He stood as ÖVP secretary-general under party leader Karl Nehammer; the ÖVP lost 11.2 points and came second behind the FPÖ. Stocker was 7th on the ÖVP federal list (Interior Ministry) and, according to profil, received 578 preferential votes at federal level. He won a regional seat in Lower Austria South.

role_sought: Member of the Wiener Neustadt municipal council (ÖVP list 'Bürgermeister-Team Klaus Schneeberger')
result: Elected; gave up his seat in February 2025
vote_share: ÖVP list: 35.8% (−9.2 points), 15 of 40 seats; turnout 52.5%
opponent: SPÖ 26.5% (11 seats), FPÖ 20.7% (8 seats), Greens 9.5% (4 seats)
detail: Held three weeks after he became acting ÖVP leader. After the election he gave up his council seat and the vice-mayoralty (German Wikipedia).

election: 41st ÖVP federal party congress: election of the federal chairman
detail: Held in Wiener Neustadt, his home town. His predecessor Karl Nehammer had been elected with 100% in 2022 (ORF).
